title: Ethiopian Lake Hawassa Fish
community: Lake Hawassa — the Rift Valley lake fish tradition
author: Chef Haile
desc: Lake Hawassa Fish — the Rift Valley tilapia preparation of Hawassa city, the most famous fish restaurant destination in Ethiopia. Fresh tilapia pan-fried with berbere and finished in a light tomato-herb sauce. The dish that brings Ethiopians and tourists alike to Hawassa's lakeside restaurants.
longDesc: Hawassa fish is the dish that built Hawassa's reputation as Ethiopia's premier fish restaurant destination — the lakeside restaurants of Hawassa, where tilapia is pulled from the lake and prepared within hours, serve what many consider the finest freshwater fish dish in Ethiopia.
ingredients: 4 whole tilapia (300g each) — cleaned, scaled, scored
// Sauce: 3 tomatoes — diced, 1 onion, 2 jalapeños, ¼ cup coriander
steps: Marinate tilapia in berbere, lemon, garlic, and salt for 20 minutes.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-high heat: 5—6 minutes per side.
In same pan: cook onion, add tomatoes and jalapeños. Cook 5 minutes.
Return fish. Spoon sauce over. Cook 3 minutes.
chefTips: Whole fish — skin and bones carry enormous flavour.
The scored skin caramelises with berbere.
cookingScience: See ETH087 for Lake Tana fish science.
sustainabilityTips: Lake Hawassa tilapia — Rift Valley lake fish from local fishermen.
healthBenefits: Rift Valley lake fish have high selenium content.
culturalNote: Hawassa fish is a pilgrimage for Ethiopian food lovers — the lakeside restaurants of Hawassa, where pelicans stand on the restaurant walls and hippos surface nearby, serve the freshest fish in Ethiopia. The combination of fresh catch, berbere, and the Rift Valley setting is one of Ethiopia's great dining experiences.
